[from /root/boxbox_surface]: DONE — boxbox-side compaction surfacing implemented and committed in the worktree.

Branch `opencode/boxbox-surface`, single commit `79dc0db` ("compaction stops being invisible on the client: boxbox reads session.compacted"), 11 files, +584/-18. Worktree clean.

## files changed (with the anchors you'll want)

**1. `lib/fleet/types.ts`**
- `:60` `sessionCompacted: "session.compacted",` added to `EventTypes` (with the session family, after `sessionDiff`).
- `:233` `export type SessionCompactedProperties` — `sessionID: string` required, everything else optional: `trigger?: "auto" | "manual"`, `overflow?: boolean`, `tokensBefore?: number`, `durationMs?: number`, `summaryChars?: number`, `tailStartID?: string`. Header comment states the fleet rule (older serves emit `{sessionID}` alone).

**2. `lib/store/fleet.tsx`**
- `:849` `export type CompactionFact = { at; trigger?; overflow?; tokensBefore?; durationMs?; tailStartID? }` — transient, this tab's memory only.
- `:863` `export function compactionFact(props, at)` — the defensive wire fold: non-number/NaN/garbage-enum/empty-string values are dropped, not coerced. Pure, so it is what the decode tests drive.
- `:908` `assembleThread(..., compaction?: CompactionFact)` — new optional 8th param, defaults to nothing.
- `:1239-1259` the application: prefers `compaction.tokensBefore` for the seam's `before`; when the seam's `after` is still the estimate it re-derives it via `postCompactionEstimate(tokensBefore, summaryTokens)` so the two numbers on one seam agree. Binding: exact match on the compaction part's `tail_start_id` when the fact carries `tailStartID`, else the newest seam. No match = no change.
- `:1702` `private compactions = new Map<string, CompactionFact>()`, cleared in `purgeSession` (`:2631`), read in `assemble()` (`:2726`).
- `:2449-2485` the `EventTypes.sessionCompacted` case: records the fact, emits `fleet.compaction`, calls `recomputeUsage(k)` only when the session is hydrated (`messagesCache`/`titleCache` hit), then `reassembleThread(k)` (itself a no-op unless the thread is open).
- `:1698` `private outputLimits` filled alongside `contextLimits` in `loadProviders` (`:2243`), and `:3253` the session row gains `compactAtPct: compactAtPct(context, output)`.

**3. `components/bb/thread/parts.tsx`** (`PitSeam`)
- `:328` new `contextDelta(part)` returns `{ shown, spoken }`: `shown` is unchanged from today (`"142k → ~8k"` / `"→ ~8k"`), `spoken` is the a11y form (`"142k to about 8k"` — an arrow and a tilde are noise out loud).
- `:391` the disclosure button's accessible name is now `"open the pit stop summary, compacted 142k to about 8k"` (and `close …` when open). With no numbers it is byte-identical to the old name. Zero visual change when the data is absent.

**4. `lib/telemetry/schema.ts:377`** — one new kind `"fleet.compaction"`, doc + props `trigger` (TEXT, values auto/manual), `overflow` (INTEGER 0/1), `tokensBefore`, `durationMs`, `summaryChars` (all INTEGER, none required). Producer is the store's event handler. `lib/telemetry/db.test.ts:118` gains its row in `oneOfEach` so the per-kind view coverage test actually exercises it.

**5. `lib/fleet/usage.ts:52`** — `compactAtPct(contextLimit, outputLimit?)`: `reserved = min(20_000, output ?? 32_000)`, `round((context − reserved) / context × 100)`, `undefined` when there is no context limit, when the reserve eats the window, or when it rounds to ≥100 (a tick at the bar's end is a lie about precision). `components/bb/thread/thread-view.tsx:46-92` FuelGauge takes `compactAt?`, draws a 1px `bg-noir` cut positioned at `left: N%` inside a now-`relative` track, gated on `pct > 0`. Existing color thresholds and bar behavior untouched; aria-label and title gain `", compacts at N%"` / `" · compacts at N%"` only when the tick renders. Wired at `:544`.

**6. `GOTCHAS.md`** — one entry (worktree scar tissue): `bunx tsc --noEmit` in a never-built worktree reports three phantom `Cannot find name 'RouteContext'` errors from `app/api/hosts/**/route.ts` because tsconfig includes `.next/types/**/*.ts`; tier 0 is only trustworthy after one `bun run build`. Verified both ways this session.

## verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean, exit 0 (after one `bun run build` generated `.next/types`; see the GOTCHAS entry).
- `bun run test` (`bun test lib`) — **621 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail**, 1525 expects. Bare `bun test` (adds `board/test`) — 716 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail.
- New tests: `lib/store/compaction.test.ts` (12 tests) — wire fixtures minimal `{sessionID}` and full enriched payload, both `satisfies SessionCompactedProperties`, decoded through `compactionFact`; a garbage-props test; seam tests for no-fact-equals-today, windowed thread gaining its before, serve count beating the derived one, the next real turn still owning `after`, `tailStartID` binding to its own seam among two, an unmatched tail id changing nothing, and a numberless fact touching nothing. `lib/fleet/usage.test.ts:146` — 6 `compactAtPct` cases (20k cap, small output limit, 32k fallback, no limit, reserve-swallows-window, rounds-to-100).
- `bun run build` — passes, "Compiled successfully in 6.3s", 27/27 static pages.
- **Screenshots: N/A.** Tier-2 visual verification against a real serve was explicitly out of scope and was NOT done. Nothing here has been driven against a live `cmx serve`; I have not seen the tick or the enriched seam render. No claim of "verified" beyond typecheck/unit/build.

## spec deviations (3, all small)

1. **Added `tailStartID` to the fact** (your list was `{at, trigger, overflow, tokensBefore, durationMs}`). Reason: without it the fact can only bind to "the newest seam", which mis-stamps an old seam for a beat when the event arrives before the new compaction request message reaches the cache. The tail id makes the binding exact; the last-seam rule remains the fallback for serves that enrich only some fields. If you want the fact minimal, drop `tailStartID` from `CompactionFact` (fleet.tsx:849), the `pitTails` map (`:956`) and the branch at `:1249` — the two tail-id tests in compaction.test.ts go with it.
2. **`durationMs` is a props column, not the envelope `ms`.** Followed your prop list verbatim, but note schema.ts's own envelope rule ("if a prop is worth filtering or grouping by across kinds, promote it to the envelope") and the `ms` doc ("duration in ms where the event has one") both point at `ms`. One-line change if you prefer the envelope; I did not emit both, duplication would be worse.
3. **Seam copy is unchanged; only the accessible name gained the words.** The visible seam already rendered `"compacted · everything above is folded into a summary"` with `"142k → ~8k"` right-aligned, so "show compacted before → after" was already satisfied visually — the enrichment is that the numbers now appear in cases where the window can't derive them, and that the a11y name carries them.

Two facts worth knowing for your server-side side: the client reads `tail_start_id` off the compaction PART for binding, so the event's `tailStartID` must be that same id to match; and `summaryChars` is telemetry-only on this side (nothing renders it). I deliberately did NOT add a GOTCHAS entry for the enriched wire shape — it isn't live-verified yet, and GOTCHAS is for paid-for knowledge. Worth adding once an enriched serve is deployed, along with re-pinning the full fixture in compaction.test.ts (its header says so).

Bohr's implementation came through with worktree isolation on the `opencode/boxbox-surface` branch, 621+ tests passing and a clean build, though tier-2 support isn't finished yet. The tailStartID binding is working well with exact matching, and it aligns perfectly with the server payload I'm sending — the compaction part's tail_start_id is there, and my publish logic correctly uses the selected.tail value.

The durationMs approach as a prop versus envelope milliseconds is fine as-is. Their branch isn't merged yet — I'm keeping the commits intact and will merge locally after cross-verification, but I won't push to main since that triggers a live deployment. The order matters: cmx fleet needs to deploy first, then boxbox can follow. the owner will handle the actual push when the server side is ready.

Now I'm rerunning the cmx typecheck, then moving to the next item.
The worktree branch is green with 621 passing tests, though server-side verification is still pending. Now I'll rerun the typecheck to continue validation.

The typecheck passes, so I'm moving on to write the prefire tests. I need two test cases: one verifying that prefire caches a note and only anchors the delta on pass-2, and another checking that a stale prefire with a pruned head falls back to full history. For the second test, I'll need a helper to create an assistant with a completed tool part so I can apply a prune-stamp to it. I'm setting up a new describe block for session.compaction.prefire and writing both tests.

For test 1, I'm seeding eight message pairs with a wide provider (100k context, 32k output, prefire band at 72k-80k), pushing a reply containing a healthy summary plus a marker, then calling prefire with specific token counts. After that, I'll push another reply for pass-2, add a new user turn, and process everything through SessionCompaction with auto disabled. The assertions check that the result continues, the captured output contains the marker inside the previous-summary tag, and early head text like turn 0 is absent.

For test 2, I'm using the same setup but this time with prefire cached, then mutating an early assistant message by adding a tool part helper function that updates a message with a completed tool execution result.

I need to check the exact ToolPart schema shape from the existing test suite to match the structure correctly — specifically the tool, callID, and state fields with their nested time and metadata properties. Once I seed the assistant message with a tool part, I'll mark it as compacted to simulate a pruned state, then verify that pass-2 captures the full head text and the new summary prompt without the previous note.

For the test itself, I'm confirming that the tool part stays in HEAD at prefire time, the stamp covers the right slice range, and that mutations in pair 0 properly break the invariant. The prefire's filterCompactedEffect reads messages from the database through the runtime service, the user.findLast lookup works, and the LLM stub queue processes both the initial reply and the second reply with the capture — making sure the captured messages are stringified correctly like in the anchor test.

Now I'm working through the pass-2 delta: after prefire runs on 8 pairs, a new user turn gets added, and at process time the select function runs over the full history. With 9 user turns total and the tail keeping the last 2 turns within the 8k limit, the tail should be around turns 8-9 while the head covers pairs 0-6 or so. But prefire ran before that new turn was added, so its select over just 8 pairs would've put the tail at pairs 6-7, meaning cachedHead would've been pairs 0-5.

At process time with the new turn, the head becomes pairs 0-6 (14 messages), and I can find where the cached head ends by looking at the index of pair 5's assistant message — that's at index 11, so the delta is just pair 6 (2 messages). I'm verifying this worked by checking that the captured text includes "turn 6" but not "turn 0", which confirms the delta was correctly isolated.

There's a potential issue with token estimates varying and shifting the tail boundary, which could make pair 6 end up in the tail instead, leaving delta empty and breaking the assertion. But since the estimates are deterministic based on character count divided by 4, the boundaries should stay fixed for these fixed texts. I'll keep the assertions as-is and adjust if needed after the first run.

Now I need to look at Euler's recall test to find the exact completed-tool-part literal so I can avoid guessing at the schema, then write the tests.
Typecheck clean. Prefire tests need a completed tool-part fixture — euler's recall test already built exactly that shape, so borrowing its literal:

+describe("session.compaction.prefire", () => {
+  // Inside the prefire band for wide(): usable = 100k - min(20k, 32k) = 80k, lead 0.9 → [72k, 80k).
+  const leading = {
+    total: 0,
+    input: 75_000,
+    output: 0,
+    reasoning: 0,
+    cache: { read: 0, write: 0 },
+  }
+  const NOTE1 = HEALTHY_SUMMARY + "\n- NOTE-ONE-MARKER"
+
+  async function seed(sessionID: SessionID, root: string, pairs = 8) {
+    const replies: MessageV2.Assistant[] = []
+    for (let i = 0; i < pairs; i++) {
+      const u = await user(sessionID, `turn ${i} with enough words that the head is clearly substantial`)
+      replies.push(await assistant(sessionID, u.id, root))
+    }
+    return replies
+  }
+
+  test("caches a background note and pass-2 anchors only the delta", async () => {
+    const stub = llm()
+    let captured = ""
+    stub.push(reply(NOTE1))
+    stub.push(
+      reply(HEALTHY_SUMMARY, (input) => {
+        captured = JSON.stringify(input.messages)
+      }),
+    )
+    const provider = wide()
+    await using tmp = await tmpdir()
+    await WithInstance.provide({
+      directory: tmp.path,
+      fn: async () => {
+        const session = await svc.create({})
+        await seed(session.id, tmp.path)
+        const rt = liveRuntime(stub.layer, provider)
+        try {
+          await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.prefire({ sessionID: session.id, tokens: leading, model: ref }),
+            ),
+          )
+
+          await user(session.id, "the newest turn after prefire")
+          await SessionCompaction.create({ sessionID: session.id, agent: "build", model: ref, auto: false })
+          const msgs = await svc.messages({ sessionID: session.id })
+          const parent = msgs.at(-1)?.info.id
+          const result = await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.process({ parentID: parent!, messages: msgs, sessionID: session.id, auto: false }),
+            ),
+          )
+          expect(result).toBe("continue")
+          expect(captured).toContain("<previous-summary>")
+          expect(captured).toContain("NOTE-ONE-MARKER")
+          expect(captured).not.toContain("turn 0 with")
+          const summaries = (await svc.messages({ sessionID: session.id })).filter(
+            (m) => m.info.role === "assistant" && m.info.summary,
+          )
+          expect(summaries.length).toBe(1)
+          expect(summaries[0]!.info.role === "assistant" && summaries[0]!.info.error).toBeUndefined()
+        } finally {
+          await rt.dispose()
+        }
+      },
+    })
+  })
+
+  test("skips outside the lead band and refuses a degenerate note", async () => {
+    const stub = llm()
+    stub.push(reply("tiny note"))
+    const provider = wide()
+    await using tmp = await tmpdir()
+    await WithInstance.provide({
+      directory: tmp.path,
+      fn: async () => {
+        const session = await svc.create({})
+        await seed(session.id, tmp.path)
+        const rt = liveRuntime(stub.layer, provider)
+        try {
+          // Below the band: no LLM call is made (queue would be consumed otherwise).
+          await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.prefire({
+                sessionID: session.id,
+                tokens: { ...leading, input: 10_000 },
+                model: ref,
+              }),
+            ),
+          )
+          // Inside the band: consumes the queued degenerate note but refuses to cache it,
+          // so a later compaction summarizes the full history.
+          await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.prefire({ sessionID: session.id, tokens: leading, model: ref }),
+            ),
+          )
+          let captured = ""
+          stub.push(
+            reply(HEALTHY_SUMMARY, (input) => {
+              captured = JSON.stringify(input.messages)
+            }),
+          )
+          await SessionCompaction.create({ sessionID: session.id, agent: "build", model: ref, auto: false })
+          const msgs = await svc.messages({ sessionID: session.id })
+          const parent = msgs.at(-1)?.info.id
+          const result = await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.process({ parentID: parent!, messages: msgs, sessionID: session.id, auto: false }),
+            ),
+          )
+          expect(result).toBe("continue")
+          expect(captured).toContain("turn 0 with")
+          expect(captured).not.toContain("NOTE-ONE-MARKER")
+          expect(captured).not.toContain("<previous-summary>")
+        } finally {
+          await rt.dispose()
+        }
+      },
+    })
+  })
+
+  test("a pruned head part invalidates the cached note and pass-2 falls back to the full history", async () => {
+    const stub = llm()
+    stub.push(reply(NOTE1))
+    let captured = ""
+    stub.push(
+      reply(HEALTHY_SUMMARY, (input) => {
+        captured = JSON.stringify(input.messages)
+      }),
+    )
+    const provider = wide()
+    await using tmp = await tmpdir()
+    await WithInstance.provide({
+      directory: tmp.path,
+      fn: async () => {
+        const session = await svc.create({})
+        const replies = await seed(session.id, tmp.path)
+        const early = replies[0]!
+        const part = await svc.updatePart({
+          id: PartID.ascending(),
+          messageID: early.id,
+          sessionID: session.id,
+          type: "tool",
+          callID: "call_" + early.id,
+          tool: "exec_command",
+          state: {
+            status: "completed",
+            input: {},
+            output: "some old tool output",
+            title: "exec_command",
+            metadata: {},
+            time: { start: Date.now(), end: Date.now() },
+          },
+        })
+        const rt = liveRuntime(stub.layer, provider)
+        try {
+          await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.prefire({ sessionID: session.id, tokens: leading, model: ref }),
+            ),
+          )
+          // Simulate the pruner touching a head part after pass-1 ran.
+          if (part.type === "tool" && part.state.status === "completed") {
+            part.state.time.compacted = Date.now()
+            await svc.updatePart(part)
+          }
+          await SessionCompaction.create({ sessionID: session.id, agent: "build", model: ref, auto: false })
+          const msgs = await svc.messages({ sessionID: session.id })
+          const parent = msgs.at(-1)?.info.id
+          const result = await rt.runPromise(
+            SessionCompaction.Service.use((svc) =>
+              svc.process({ parentID: parent!, messages: msgs, sessionID: session.id, auto: false }),
+            ),
+          )
+          expect(result).toBe("continue")
+          expect(captured).toContain("turn 0 with")
+          expect(captured).not.toContain("NOTE-ONE-MARKER")
+        } finally {
+          await rt.dispose()
+        }
+      },
+    })
+  })
+})

Both test failures point to the same issue: `captured` ends up empty because the pass-2 capture reply was never actually consumed. The root cause seems to be that prefire returned early without making an LLM call, which means the process function would consume the first stub item directly without triggering the capture function, leaving `captured` blank. I'm trying to figure out why prefire would exit early in the first place.

Walking through the gate conditions: compaction config is undefined, so most early-exit checks fail. The compaction agent does exist and resolves its model correctly—the test provider has the right model ID and provider ID set up. The token count calculation looks right too: with zero leading tokens, it falls back to the sum of 75,000. Now I'm checking the usable calculation: the model has 100k context and 32k output, so reserved tokens would be 20,000, and I need to verify the remaining usable space calculation.

Actually, I'm realizing the usable formula depends on whether limit.input is defined. When it's absent, usable equals context minus maxOutputTokens, which gives 100,000 − 32,000 = 68,000, not 80,000 like I thought. That means my leading input of 75,000 exceeds the usable band and would trigger compaction—but prefire correctly skips it because the config disables it. My test math was off; I need to adjust the leading input to 65,000 to stay within the valid band and fix the comment to reflect the actual calculation.

Now I'm checking the other test values: the second test's 10k below-band value is fine, and I need to fix the pruned-part literal issue by restructuring how I reference it. The degenerate-note test's band value already uses leading correctly, and for the "caches..." test, once I fix the leading value, prefire should run and consume the note before caching, which the second reply will then capture.

I found the issue — the band math was using the wrong `usable()` branch, which calculated usable tokens as 68k instead of 80k, causing the 75k token capture to sit above the band and get skipped. I'll fix the fixture tokens and the prune-part literal.

The root sessions are registered at "/root", and I need to figure out how to handle the ROOT session case—whether it has a registered path or if I should default to an empty string when metadata isn't available.

For sessions that haven't spawned any children yet, there's no PerRootData entry, so listAgents might error or return an empty array. I'm thinking of wrapping this defensively with a catch handler that returns an empty list on AgentPathInvalidError. Then I need to wire up the Todo service to fetch the session's todo items with their content and status, which means importing SessionTodo into prompt.ts and adding it to the layer dependencies—though that requires finding the SessionPrompt layer definition first. Alternatively, I could gather the live state in the COMPACTION service instead to keep the changes smaller.

Actually, prompt.ts already has agentControl in scope from drainMailbox, so I only need to add the todo dependency. For the AgentPath construction, I can follow the same pattern as agent-list.ts—use getAgentMetadata to resolve the current path, falling back to the AgentPath root constant if needed. Then I need to locate the prompt.ts layer definition and its defaultLayer list to add the new dependencies.

Now I'm setting up the compaction input to accept a liveState array, and building that state in the dispatch handler by calling a local helper that collects agent metadata...

Building the helper function... Writing compaction logic... For manual compaction, there's no injection since the human is in control. I need to write tests for the auto-continue path: when auto is enabled and we're not replaying, the processor should inject the state block with the recall pointer. I'll extend the existing test to verify that processing with auto-continue includes the live state snapshot and recall tool reference in the continue text, then check whether the current assertions need updating since the new block changes the prefix format.

The prompt helper for compacting live state is best covered at the service level rather than unit-testing the prompt layer directly—the glue code is straightforward enough to review by inspection. I'm adding `liveState?: string[]` to the process input interface, then tracing through the agent-list tool pattern, the prompt layer dependencies, and the existing continue test assertions to make sure everything aligns.
Shapes confirmed. Three more reads to wire it exactly — the agent-list tool's path idiom, prompt.ts's layer deps, and the existing continue-prompt assertions I must not break:

I need to set up the imports in prompt.ts to bring in SessionTodo from the todo module, checking whether it's a direct export or needs the namespace import pattern, then add the todo yield statement after the agentControl yield to integrate it into the control flow.

Next I'll handle the helper function and dispatch edits around line 1844, update the defaultLayer at 2181 to include SessionTodo.defaultLayer in the Layer.suspend pipe, and then work on compaction.ts to capture the live state of both the agent control tree and todo list at compaction time so the model can re-anchor properly after resuming.

I'm defining a helper function that snapshots the current agent state and todo list... I'm working through the type system here — the agents array comes back as either a readonly ListedAgent[] or an empty readonly array, and TypeScript handles both cases fine in the for-of loop. For the todos, the Info type is defined as a Schema struct in the todo module, and when I call get() it returns an Effect that resolves to an Info[] array, where Info serves double duty as both the schema definition and the inferred type.

Rather than explicitly annotating the type, I'll use Effect.succeed with an empty array and let TypeScript infer the union — that way if Info isn't exported as a type, the inference still works and filters correctly. The AgentToolContext.currentAgentPath returns an Effect that I can chain into, and then I'm handling the dispatch logic for the compaction task type.

- L398 `bus-subscribe-helper-vs-service-method-cross-runtime-mismatch` — top-level vs in-effect subscribe target different PubSubs in `testEffect`.
- L419 `bus-subscriber-needs-instance-state-fork-and-instance-ref` — long-lived subscribers must fork inside `InstanceState.make` AND re-inject `InstanceRef`.
- L887 `syncevent-publish-uses-top-level-bus-runtime` — events from `SyncEvent.run` land on the top-level Bus runtime, not your test layer's.
- L868 `syncevent-publish-uses-helper-bus-not-test-layer-bus` — same root cause from the other side: subscribe via top-level `Bus.subscribe` from inside `InstanceState.make`.
- L138 `agentcontrol-providerref-must-live-in-layer-not-instancestate` — single-value, instance-agnostic state belongs at layer scope, not in `InstanceState`.
- L148 `agentcontrol-d5-extractor-needs-two-pass-walk-for-terse-followup-status-line` — D5 completion watcher must prefer non-terse bodies before falling back to terse status lines.
- L181 `agentcontrol-d11-abort-line-parser-last-line-only` — parse ABORT set-phrase anchored to LAST non-empty line; interior or quoted ABORT mentions must NOT trigger.
### Sourced events
- L551 `eventv2-and-bus-dual-emission-with-parallel-type-prefixes` — keep EventV2 (`session.next.<domain>.…`) and BusEvent (`<domain>.…`) under different type prefixes; emit both with the same payload.
### Session run loop
- L966 `session-runloop-lock-busy-guard-was-per-instance` — the busy guard was in-memory per-instance while the sqlite is host-global; two instances (or a tui + serve) could run one session's loop concurrently. `SessionRunState.ensureRunning` now wraps the loop in a host-scoped `EffectFlock` lock.
### Tool definitions
- L954 `tool-define-execute-r-must-be-never-capture-services-in-closure` — lifting helpers out of `Tool.define` widens execute's R; capture services in the outer closure and provide inline.
- L995 `tool-define-inner-effect-gen-closing-brace` — wrapping the spec in an inner `Effect.gen` leaves a `})` line at 0 hits.
- L1024 `tool-execute-needs-explicit-result-type-disjoint-metadata` — multi-branch `execute` with disjoint metadata needs `Effect.Effect<Tool.ExecuteResult>` annotation.
- L918 `tool-context-ask-typed-as-void` — `ctx.ask` is typed `Effect<void>` but raises at runtime; use `Effect.acquireUseRelease` for cleanup.
- L172 `agentcontrol-required-by-toolregistry-existing-test-layers` — adding a new dep to `ToolRegistry.layer` silently breaks every custom test layer.
- L257 `bench-tool-yield-loses-transitive-deps` — yielding a tool factory directly skips transitive deps; route through `ToolRegistry.tools(...)`.
- L613 `multi-ask-capture-needs-counter` — capture helpers that throw on the first `ctx.ask` truncate multi-ask tool flows; gate the throw on a counter.
### PTY
- L891 `pty-exited-model-session-pins-ptmx-fds` — an exited model PTY keeps two `/dev/ptmx` fds until `kill()`; the per-directory LRU cap can never fire under worktree fan-out, so the host hits `kern.tty.ptmx_max` and ALL pty spawns fail.
- L770 `pty-onexit-auto-remove-tui-only` — `proc.onExit` auto-removal must gate on `origin === "tui"` so model PTYs survive for post-exit drain.
- L748 `pty-create-term-override-tui-only` — `Pty.create`'s `TERM=xterm-256color` overlay must gate on `origin === "tui"`.
- L731 `pty-bench-baseline-vs-new-work` — combining new work into an existing baseline metric is apples-to-oranges; split metrics.
- L1013 `tty-line-discipline-echo-defeats-clamp-timing-tests` — TTY echo wakes `Pty.read` early; verify clamps at the unit level.
- L1418 `pty-leader-exit-sighup-vs-nohup-race` — `&` children die at leader exit; nohup races its own signal setup; use `detach: true`.
- L1429 `pty-read-collect-until-deadline-holds-full-window` — data-present reads hold the full window since 2026-07-18; idleMs <= 0 drains instantly.
### Bench methodology
- L663 `opentui-render-bench-noise-needs-best-of-n` — opentui `renderOnce` benches need best-of-3 to suppress noise.
- L637 `opentui-multi-text-node-vs-single-baseline-cap` — N separate `<text>` nodes inherently exceed a single-text baseline by ~1.5×; use `<text><span/>...<span/></text>`.
- L792 `runloop-bench-vs-baseline-methodology-mismatch` — in-`Effect.gen` microbenches and per-sample-`runPromise` baselines measure different things.
- L468 `e2e-perf-sibling-fanout-needs-median-of-n` — single-iteration timing flakes under a noisy suite; median-of-5 minimum.
- L688 `opentui-testRender-leak` — `testRender` allocates native resources; always `handle.renderer.destroy()`.
### TUI rendering
- L1059 `tui-flex-row-with-tall-text` — `<box flexDirection="row">` containing a tall `<text>` child silently freezes opentui paint.
- L1035 `tui-component-coverage-needs-mount-split` — split hooks-using TUI components into helpers+view + wrapper to reach 100% line cov.

- L708 `permission-disabled-removes-tool-from-active-set` — wildcard `permission: deny` strips the tool entirely; the `ctx.ask` path never fires.
- L1140 `permission-fixture-order-rule-must-precede-specific-via-findlast` — fixtures with `*: ask` AFTER `git *: allow` produce ask, NOT allow; findLast picks the LAST match.

input.newString:
### `dev-serve-event-sse-closes-after-first-frame`

**Severity:** DX-trap

- **When:** driving SSE (`GET /event`) against a serve started from the checkout with `bun run dev serve ...` (dev channel), e.g. to live-verify a new bus event.
- **Symptom:** the stream delivers exactly one `server.connected` frame and then the server closes the connection — no heartbeats, no session events, `curl -N` exits 0 immediately. Passing `?directory=` explicitly changes nothing. Looks exactly like your event change broke the stream.
- **Fix:** don't bisect your diff — a clean tree behaves identically (verified 2026-08-20 on `6330f4abe3`). Verify new bus events at the unit tier (`Bus.Service.subscribeCallback` against a real publish — the same PubSub the SSE route forwards), and verify literal wire frames against a channel-build serve, where `/event` streams fine (boxbox runs on it daily).
- **Why:** root cause not chased to ground; the dev serve's stderr shows a partial `AsyncLocalStorage` trace when the stream opens, suggesting instance-context resolution dies in the dev-run backend path. Specific to `bun run dev` — installed channel builds are unaffected.
- **See:** `packages/opencode/test/session/compaction.test.ts` ("publishes compacted event on continue") for the unit-tier wire assertion pattern.

### `layer-pipe-20-arg-cap-collapses-types-to-unknown`

**Severity:** DX-trap

- **When:** adding one more `Layer.provide(...)` to an already-long `.pipe(...)` chain — the big `defaultLayer` assemblies (`SessionPrompt.defaultLayer` is at the cap today).
- **Symptom:** one `TS2554: Expected 0-20 arguments, but got 21` at the pipe — buried under a CASCADE of misleading errors in far-away files: `Layer<Service, unknown, unknown> is not assignable ...` in the server assembly, app-runtime, tests, and scripts, all reading like missing service dependencies.
- **Fix:** fold the new layer into an existing `Layer.mergeAll(...)` argument inside the chain instead of adding a 21st pipe argument. When you see an `unknown`-typed Layer/Effect cascade, grep the typecheck output for `TS2554` first and fix that root; the rest evaporates.
- **Why:** `pipe`'s overloads are typed up to 20 arguments. Past that, TS resolves no overload, the whole pipe expression degrades to `unknown`, and every downstream consumer of the layer inherits `unknown` error/requirement channels — the diagnostics point at the consumers, not the pipe.
- **See:** `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` (`defaultLayer` — `Todo.defaultLayer` folded into the trailing `Layer.mergeAll` rather than piped).

parts.text: All the agents have finished their work, so now I need to write up the final report with complete sentences, making sure to re-ground everything in the actual findings, document what we achieved with supporting evidence, be honest about what's still open, and note that the deployment decision rests with him.

Done. Everything green-lit is built, tested, and verified as far as this machine allows. Here's the state of both repos.

## what landed in cmx (`~/code/cmx`, uncommitted on `cmx` branch)

**Degenerate-summary floor** — a compaction summary now gets validated before it becomes load-bearing: empty is always rejected; under 500 chars or missing the template's `## Goal` is rejected when the summarized head is substantial (≥6 messages) and the built-in prompt was used. One fresh retry; a second failure errors the attempt without splicing, so a garbage summary can never become the anchor that poisons every future compaction. `src/session/compaction.ts`.

**Sticky failure suppression** — "too large to compact" or double-degenerate now sets a per-session suppress flag (module-scoped, because the routes, loop, and module exports run in different Effect runtimes — layer scope would have split the state). Auto-compaction stops re-attempting a deterministic failure; a model switch, a manual `/compact`, or a later success clears it.

**Prefire two-pass** — the latency killer. At 90% of the usable window the run loop forks a background pass-1 (no session messages, no events) that summarizes the current head and caches the note with a prefix fingerprint (message ids + part counts + prune stamps). When compaction actually fires, pass-2 anchors that note as the `<previous-summary>` and summarizes only the delta — the blocking call prefills a few turns instead of the whole history. Staleness (revert, prune, model switch) falls back to single-pass silently; a degenerate retry drops the cache and rebuilds from the full head. Config: `compaction.prefire` (default on). Entries are prefix-validated, so one prefire serves a whole compaction cycle rather than re-firing every turn.

**Structural post-compaction reminder** — the auto-continue turn now opens with a `<post-compaction-state>` block carrying live subagents (read from `AgentControl`'s tree) and open todos (read from the todo table), gathered by the loop and passed in as plain input — no new layer edge on compaction. The recall pointer rides it always.

**`recall` tool** (delegated, delivered) — session-scoped search over the full stored history, including compacted-away messages and pruned tool outputs (whose text survives in the rows). Registered across all four registry surfaces plus the tool-list snapshot allowlist.

401: own docs say so). the systemd unit is untouched — `ExecStart` already
402: points at `bun run start`.
403: 
404: the production path is deliberately bun-native (`NODE_ENV=production bun
405: server.ts`): **the box has no node at all**, and `bun run` silently
406: substitutes bun wherever a script says `node`, so a node-based start
407: script crash-loops the service instead of failing loudly. dev is the
408: exception and stays on node (`node --import tsx server.ts`) because
409: turbopack panics under bun when it spawns its pooled postcss process —
410: dev only ever runs on the mac, which has node.
411: 
412: the drain still holds with terminals attached: sigterm with a live
413: terminal socket exits in ~50ms (the 90s white screen stays dead).
414: 
415: 
416: ## config changes: no restarts, ever (2026-07-19)
417: 
418: cmx builds >= `d262514989` hot-reload config. the serve watches
419: `~/.config/opencode` (and project config files where the experimental
420: watcher is on) and propagates edits live: broken files are ignored until
421: they parse (previous config stays active), mcp/lsp/plugin only restart
422: when their slice actually changed, running turns finish on the config
423: they started with, and every reload publishes `config.updated` over sse
424: (boxbox can surface it). sessions, ptys, and pending permissions are
425: untouched.
426: 
427: adding a skill / mcp / agent to the fleet is therefore just:
428: 
429: ```sh
430: # edit ~/.config/opencode on the mac, then
431: rsync -a --delete --exclude node_modules --exclude .DS_Store ~/.config/opencode/ boxbox:.config/opencode/
432: rsync -a --delete --exclude node_modules --exclude .DS_Store ~/.config/opencode/ forge-vm:.config/opencode/
433: ```
434: 
435: serves converge within ~1s of the rsync landing. verified live
436: 2026-07-19: skill add + delete propagated to all three machines with
437: zero restarts, `config.updated` frames captured on `/global/event`.
438: 
439: ## upgrading the cmx binary
440: 
441: the one thing that still needs restarts. **and the rule paid for on
442: 2026-07-23, round four of four: a serve restart aborts every in-flight
443: agent turn on that machine, and dev LIVES on this fleet — before ANY
444: restart wave, check whether he's active (live laps on the serves, him
445: driving boxbox) and ASK unless he just ordered the deploy. deploy-numb
446: is a real failure mode: rounds one through three were ordered and fine,
447: round four fired into his working session.** when you rebuild the cmx
448: binary (new build into `~/.local/bin`), the running serve keeps the old
449: CODE until restarted:
450: 
451: ```sh
452: systemctl --user restart cmx-serve      # the vm's own workbench serve
453: ```
454: 
455: linux upgrade flow as executed 2026-07-22: both vms carry their own cmx
456: clone and the serve execs the repo's OWN dist output (boxbox wrapper →
457: `~/cmx/packages/opencode/dist/opencode-linux-x64/bin/opencode`;
458: forge is nested one deeper, `~/cmx/cmx/...`). so the
459: upgrade is: build on-box, restart after green —
460: 
461: ```sh
462: ssh boxbox 'export PATH=$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH; cd ~/cmx && git pull --ff-only && bun install && ./packages/opencode/script/build.ts --single && systemctl --user restart cmx-serve'
463: ```
464: 
465: `--single` builds the native platform only; the script's smoke test
466: prints the new version. linux does not care that the running serve's
467: binary gets unlinked mid-build (orphaned inode) — restart only AFTER
468: the build goes green, so a failed build leaves the old serve running.
469: 
470: verifying a deploy end-to-end: `cmx run` over ssh MUST have stdin
471: closed (`ssh -n`, or `< /dev/null`) — with the ssh channel holding
472: stdin open, `cmx run` parks forever right after bootstrap, and a
473: `timeout ... | tail` pipe masks the 124 as exit 0. burned an hour on
474: 2026-07-25 chasing a phantom model hang that was neither cmx nor the
475: proxy:
476: 
477: ```sh
478: ssh -n boxbox 'export PATH=$HOME/.bun/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH; cd /tmp && cmx run -m anthropic/claude-opus-5 "reply with exactly: ok" < /dev/null'
479: ```
480: 
481: the other serves: forge `systemctl --user restart cmx-serve`, mac
482: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/systems.example-org.cmx-serve` —
483: or just the restart button on the machines screen, which is the same
484: thing without a terminal.
485: 
486: **COMMIT FIRST, always (dev's law, 2026-07-23).** the linux boxes
487: build from their clones of origin, so they CANNOT ship uncommitted
488: code — but the mac builds from the LOCAL working tree, and every mac
489: binary shipped on 2026-07-23 silently carried a dirty-tree fix the vms
490: lacked: same version family, forked fleet, the exact ghost this doc
491: exists to prevent. the mac build step is only legal on a CLEAN tree
492: sitting at origin HEAD (`git status --short` empty, `git log -1` on
493: origin). commit → push → build → deploy, no exceptions, no "it's just
494: my tree".
495: 
496: mac install pattern, load-bearing (learned 2026-07-19 the long way):the serve binary is COPIED to `~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode` and the
497: `~/.local/bin/cmx` wrapper execs THAT, never the build output in
498: `~/Documents`. two different tcc traps otherwise: a launchd spawn of a
499: binary living under `~/Documents` stalls MINUTES in dyld (consent
500: machinery a background process can't answer), and a binary outside
501: `~/Documents` without full disk access hangs FOREVER on its first read
502: into a Documents-scoped repo (openat parks, 0% cpu, instance routes dead
503: while non-instance routes answer). the fix is both halves: binary at the
504: stable `~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode` path + a ONE-TIME full disk
505: access grant for that path (system settings, privacy & security, full
506: disk access). rebuilds land at the same path and inherit the grant.
507: mac redeploy is therefore: build, `cp` into `~/.local/share/cmx/bin/`,
508: kickstart. spawns take ~4s.
509: 
510: **the cp must be IN PLACE (same inode), and the serve must be DOWN when
511: it lands (2026-07-20, both halves bit the same deploy):**
512: 
513: - an atomic rename-swap (`cp new tmp && mv -f tmp opencode`) creates a
514:   NEW inode and the fda grant does not follow it: the next launchd spawn
515:   parks forever in `openat$NOCANCEL` (the exact hang above), and only a
516:   manual fda re-toggle in system settings revives it. "rebuilds inherit
517:   the grant" is true of in-place `cp` only.
518: - but an in-place `cp` while any process is EXECUTING the binary makes
519:   macos SIGKILL fresh spawns of it (in-place write invalidates the code
520:   signature; exit 137 on the very next `cmx --version`). running serves
521:   keep their mapped pages and survive, but nothing new launches cleanly
522:   until the write finishes.
523: 
524: so the ritual, in order: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/systems.example-org.cmx-serve`
525: (or at minimum accept the kill), `cp` OVER the existing file, bootstrap/
526: kickstart. never rename-swap this path.
527: 
528: **and the serve is not the only executor (2026-07-20, second bite):**
529: tuis and harness serves exec the SAME binary. if ANY of them is alive
530: when the in-place cp lands, macos poisons the vnode's code-signing
531: state PERSISTENTLY — every fresh spawn (launchd bootstraps included)
532: dies `OS_REASON_CODESIGNING` / exit 137, and the poison survives both
533: the executors exiting AND a clean re-cp with zero executors. the heal
534: that works, same inode, fda intact:
535: 
536: ```sh
537: codesign --force --sign - ~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode
538: ```
539: 
540: prevention: before the cp, `lsof -t ~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode`
541: must print NOTHING — bootout the serve, exit every tui, kill stray
542: harness serves. and never `set -x` a script that interpolates the serve
543: password into a curl line; the first swap script logged it to /tmp.
544: 
545: **when the deployer IS an executor (2026-07-22):** an agent deployed
546: from inside a cmx process cannot satisfy "lsof prints nothing" — its own
547: pid holds the binary. the variant that worked: bootout the serve, gate
548: on `lsof -t` printing EXACTLY the deployer's pid (abort on anything
549: else), in-place `cp`, then IMMEDIATELY `codesign --force --sign -`
550: before any fresh spawn. spawns came out clean (no 137). but the heal's
551: "fda intact" claim did NOT hold that day: the serve came up listening
552: and parked FOREVER in `openat$NOCANCEL` (0% cpu, every route timing
553: out — diagnose with `sample <pid> 1`). the ad-hoc re-sign changes the
554: cdhash, and tcc apparently keyed the grant to it. assume any
555: executor-alive swap costs the manual fda re-toggle (system settings,
556: privacy & security, full disk access, toggle the entry off and on),
557: then `launchctl kickstart -k`. plan mac deploys accordingly: the swap
558: is agent-safe, the revival needs hands.
559: 
560: ## the FDA re-grant ends here: sign with a STABLE identity (2026-07-23)
561: 
562: the whole re-toggle tax above is one root cause: **ad-hoc signatures
563: have no stable identity, so tcc keys the fda grant to the cdhash, and
564: every rebuild is a new cdhash = a stranger.** the fix is to re-sign the
565: deployed mac binary with a real, stable code-signing identity. dev's
566: mac already has an `Apple Development` cert (from xcode); its designated
567: requirement is cert-based, not cdhash-based, so a grant survives every
568: rebuild signed with the same cert. this also kills the per-folder
569: consent popups on the serve lineage (same root: no stable principal).
570: 
571: one-time setup (already done 2026-07-23):
572: 
573: - find the identity: `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` →
574:   `Apple Development: owner@example.com (KLMNO13579)`.
575: - if `codesign` fails with `errSecInternalComponent`, the private key's
576:   partition list doesn't name codesign (silent block, no prompt). fix,
577:   once, with the login password:
578:   ```sh
579:   security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s \
580:     -k "<login password>" ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
581:   ```
582: - the sign must run in a GUI session (Ghostty), not an agent's exec
583:   context — the keychain authorization prompt needs a window. click
584:   **Always Allow** once.
585: - do NOT use `--options runtime` (hardened runtime): it blocks JIT and
586:   bun's JavaScriptCore crashes. plain `--sign` is what tcc keys on.
587: - grant fda ONE final time to `~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode` (remove
588:   any stale ad-hoc entry first — it's keyed to a dead cdhash).
589: 
590: the mac upgrade ritual is therefore now: bootout, in-place `cp`, then
591: 
592: ```sh
593: codesign --force --sign "Apple Development: owner@example.com (KLMNO13579)" \
594:   ~/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode
595: ```
596: 
597: then bootstrap/kickstart — **no fda toggle.** verify the DR stayed
598: cert-based (`codesign -d --requirements -` shows `certificate
599: leaf[subject.CN] = "Apple Development: …"`). the proof it worked: the
600: NEXT deploy's kickstart answers routes without a park. if a rebuild ever
601: DOES re-ask, the cert identifier or cert changed — check the DR first,
602: don't reach for the toggle. the agent can run this sign itself ONLY if
603: the key's partition list already allows codesign (post-setup); otherwise
604: it's a hands step in Ghostty.

(End of file - total 604 lines)

#!/bin/bash
# cmx mac binary swap — the ritual per boxy-web/ops/deploy.md.
# Order is load-bearing: bootout first, cp IN PLACE (same inode, never rename-swap),
# codesign with the STABLE cert immediately (executors may be alive: tuis exec this
# binary), bootstrap last. No passwords touched anywhere in this script.
UNIT=systems.example-org.cmx-serve
BIN="$HOME/.local/share/cmx/bin/opencode"
NEW="$HOME/Documents/Personal/cmx/packages/opencode/dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode"
IDENT="Apple Development: owner@example.com (KLMNO13579)"

echo "== cmx mac swap $(date) =="
"$NEW" --version || { echo "ABORT: new binary broken"; exit 1; }

launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/$UNIT" && echo "bootout ok" || echo "bootout rc=$? (unit may not be loaded)"
sleep 2

echo "-- executors still holding the binary (expected: the live tui):"
lsof -t "$BIN" || echo "(none)"

cp "$NEW" "$BIN" || { echo "ABORT: cp failed"; exit 1; }
echo "cp in place done"

codesign --force --sign "$IDENT" "$BIN" || { echo "ABORT: codesign failed"; exit 1; }
echo "signed"
codesign -d --requirements - "$BIN" 2>&1 | grep -m1 "certificate leaf"

launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/$UNIT.plist" && echo "bootstrap ok" || {
  echo "bootstrap rc=$?, trying kickstart"
  launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/$UNIT"
}

sleep 6
echo "-- fresh spawn check:"
"$BIN" --version
echo "-- unit state:"
launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/$UNIT" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "state =|pid =" | head -3
echo "== done =="

# Changes: Global server surface + config hot-reload

**Date**: 2026-07-19

Two server-side capabilities: a `/global/*` HTTP surface for host-level operations (fs browse, cache reload, restart) with the auth hole on that prefix closed, and live config hot-reload so config file edits apply without restarting the process.

## GET /global/fs + /global/* auth close (`fe92f6ab2e`)

- **`src/server/global-fs.ts` (NEW, 77 lines).** Host directory browse: lists entries for an absolute path, used by clients to pick project directories without shelling out.
- **`src/server/routes/global.ts` (NEW).** Legacy-backend `/global/*` route group.
- **httpapi backend parity.** `routes/instance/httpapi/{groups,handlers}/global.ts` (NEW) expose the same surface on the Effect HttpApi backend.
- **Auth hole closed.** `/global/*` previously bypassed bearer auth on the httpapi backend (`public.ts` treated the prefix as public). Now pinned behind auth on both backends; regression coverage in `test/server/httpapi-raw-route-auth.test.ts` (NEW) + `httpapi-bridge.test.ts`. GOTCHAS entry: `httpapi-root-api-family-needs-auth-router-middleware`.
- Tests: `test/server/global-fs.test.ts` (98 lines).

## Config hot-reload (`57fcf0e19d` + fixes `d93f208e88`, `d262514989`)

Config file changes apply live — no restart.

- **`src/config/reload.ts` (NEW, ~280 lines after fixes).** Watches config files via `file/watcher.ts`, and on change flushes the per-instance caches and re-boots the instance state so agents/commands/providers/skills/mcp/tools/lsp/format/plugins pick up the new config. One-line cache-registration hooks added across 14 service modules (`agent.ts`, `command/index.ts`, `format/index.ts`, `lsp.ts`, `mcp/index.ts`, `plugin/index.ts`, `provider/{auth,provider}.ts`, `skill/index.ts`, `tool/registry.ts`, …).
- **`effect/instance-registry.ts` + `instance-state.ts` extensions.** Flush/re-boot primitives the reloader drives; tests in `test/effect/instance-state.test.ts`.
- **Fix: never flush an in-flight boot (`d93f208e88`).** Flushing an instance mid-boot deadlocked inside ScopedCache (the flush waits on the boot which waits on the cache slot). Reload now skips in-flight boots with a bounded late-boot retry, plus a watcher noise filter (editor tmp-file churn).
- **Fix: watcher must be forced alive (`d262514989`).** Per-service runtimes are lazy — a layer nothing references is never constructed, so the watcher silently never started. `Server.listen` now explicitly touches the reload service.
- **GOTCHAS (`c1abd5e895`).** Two entries: the lazy-runtime construction trap + the ScopedCache in-flight-boot deadlock.

## POST /global/reload + /global/restart (`0d70d6f39f`)

- **`/global/reload`** flushes skills/mcp/config caches live via the reload service — the manual trigger for the same path the watcher drives.
- **`/global/restart`** (`src/server/global-lifecycle.ts`, NEW): clean process exit for the supervisor to relaunch.

# Changes: Compaction hardening — the summary stops being a single point of failure

**Date**: 2026-08-21

One drop (`b01f937a1a`): five pieces ported in judgment from xai-org/grok-build's compaction stack onto this fork's anchored-summary design, after a full read of their implementation (two-pass prefire, degenerate rejection, suppression scoping, recovery surfaces). The shared thesis: a compaction summary is a lossy bottleneck, so guard what goes in, hide the latency, and give the model structural paths back to what was dropped.

## Degenerate-summary floor (`b01f937a1a`)

A summary is validated before it becomes load-bearing. Empty is always degenerate; under 500 chars or missing the template's `## Goal` heading is degenerate when the summarized head is substantial (>= 6 messages) and the built-in prompt ran (custom `experimental.session.compacting` prompts skip the template check). One fresh retry; a second failure errors the attempt WITHOUT splicing.

- **`src/session/compaction.ts`.** `isDegenerateSummary` + the attempt-loop restructure of `processCompaction` (assistant-message creation + processor run extracted into `attempt()`, summary re-read via `readSummary`, failed attempts marked `{name: "UnknownError"}` + `finish: "error"` so `filterCompacted`/`completedCompactions` never treat them as boundaries).
- Why it matters here specifically: this fork anchors summaries — every later compaction "updates" the previous one via `<previous-summary>`, so one degenerate splice would poison the session permanently.

## Sticky failure suppression (`b01f937a1a`)

"Too large to compact even stripped" and double-degenerate set a per-session suppress flag; auto-compaction stops re-attempting a deterministic failure every turn (previously every subsequent prompt on a wedged session re-ran and re-failed the same compaction). Cleared by a model switch, a manual compact, or a later success. Manual `/compact` bypasses it.

- **`src/session/compaction.ts`.** Module-scoped `suppressed` map + `suppression()` — module scope is deliberate: the server routes, the run loop, and the module-level exports run in **different Effect runtimes**, so a layer-closure map would split state per runtime (session IDs are host-globally unique, so process scope is correct). Gates: `isOverflow` (new optional `sessionID` param, existing call sites unchanged) and `create` (auto only; manual clears).
- **`src/session/prompt.ts`.** The loop's proactive trigger passes `sessionID`.

## Prefire two-pass (`b01f937a1a`)

Compaction was a synchronous full-history summarize at full-model speed — minutes of dead air exactly on the longest autonomous runs. Now: once usage crosses 90% of the usable window, the loop forks a background pass-1 (`Effect.ignore` + `forkIn(scope)`, same shape as title generation) that summarizes the current head into a cached note — no session messages, no events. When compaction fires, pass-2 anchors the note as `<previous-summary>` and summarizes only the delta, so the blocking call prefills a few turns instead of the whole history.

- **`src/session/compaction.ts`.** `prefire` (self-gating: config, suppression, in-flight guard, threshold band, cache validity), `prefireStamp` (identity + mutation stamp: message ids, part counts, newest prune timestamp — completed turns are immutable except pruning), `prefireCut` (prefix validation), `buildInputs(useCache)` in `processCompaction` (a degenerate pass-2 drops the cache and retries from the full head). Entries are prefix-validated, not equality-validated — one prefire serves a whole compaction cycle instead of re-firing every turn in the band. Stale (revert / prune / model switch) falls back to single-pass silently. In-flight-at-compact skips rather than joins (v1 simplification; the `prefire cached` / `prefire hit` / `prefire stale` log lines are the observables for whether a join is worth adding).
- **`src/session/prompt.ts`.** The per-turn trigger after the auto-compact check.
- **`src/config/config.ts`.** `compaction.prefire` (boolean, default on) — the off-switch for the speculative spend.
- New layer dep: `LLM.Service` on `SessionCompaction` (pass-1 calls `llm.stream` directly with `tools: {}`).

## recall tool (`b01f937a1a`)

Pruned tool outputs render as `[Old tool result content cleared]` and compacted history vanishes from the model's view — but the text never leaves the sqlite rows (pruning only stamps `state.time.compacted`; rendering clears). `recall` is the pull-based escape hatch: session-scoped, case-insensitive AND-term search over the full stored history including compacted-away messages and pruned outputs (marked `[recovered from pruned tool output]`), ranked by term-hit density, ~700-char excerpts.

- **`src/tool/recall/recall.ts` + `recall.txt` (NEW, fork-only).**
- **`src/tool/registry.ts`.** Registered across the four registry surfaces; `test/integration/tool-surface-replacement.test.ts` allowlist entry per the `tool-list-snapshot-needs-post-baseline-allowlist-entry` gotcha.
- Permission shape mirrors grep (`permission: "recall"`, default allow — a `permission.recall` config lever exists but never prompts by default).

## Structural live-state on the auto-continue turn (`b01f937a1a`)

The summary template's "Live State" bullet was the only carrier of running-subagent handles and open todos across a compaction — LLM prose, best-effort. Now the auto-continue user turn opens with a `<post-compaction-state>` block built from the runtime, not the summary: live subagents from `AgentControl`'s in-memory tree, open todos from the todo table. The recall pointer always rides the block.

- **`src/session/prompt.ts`.** `compactionLiveState` — gathered by the loop (which already holds `agentControl`) and passed into `compaction.process` as plain input, deliberately avoiding a new `AgentControl` layer edge on `SessionCompaction`. New `Todo.Service` dep on `SessionPrompt` (folded into the trailing `Layer.mergeAll` — the 21st `.pipe` arg collapses the layer type to `unknown`, see the new gotcha).
- **`src/session/compaction.ts`.** `liveState?: string[]` on `process`; block assembly in the auto-continue path.

## session.compacted enrichment (`b01f937a1a`)

Payload grows `trigger` ("auto" | "manual"), `overflow`, `tokensBefore` (last real assistant usage before the compaction), `durationMs` (covers retries), `summaryChars`, `tailStartID`. All optional on the wire; pre-drop clients and serves interop cleanly. SDK regenerated (`packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/types.gen.ts`). boxbox consumes this (event union, pit-seam numbers, `fleet.compaction` telemetry, fuel-gauge threshold tick — boxy-web `b904224`).

## Tests + verification

- `test/session/compaction.test.ts`: 13 new tests (degenerate retry/suppression/model-switch clear/manual clear, prefire cache-anchors-delta / band gating / degenerate-note refusal / prune-invalidation, live-state block, enriched event assertions). The fake processor now writes a healthy template summary so fake-runtime tests exercise the accept path. 56/56.
- Full suite 4011 pass; all 11 failures attributed pre-existing or load-flake via clean-tree bisection.
- Live drive against a real serve from this checkout: real turn → real compaction (accepted) → the model called `recall` unprompted-by-tooling and recovered a compacted-away instruction.
- The 19-package turbo typecheck ran green as the pre-push hook.
- GOTCHAS: `layer-pipe-20-arg-cap-collapses-types-to-unknown`, `dev-serve-event-sse-closes-after-first-frame`.

## Deliberately not ported from grok-build

Input degradation ladder (exists there for engine-cache-aligned verbatim input; this fork already strips for the compaction call), segments mode (recall covers it), compaction checkpoints (storage here never deletes), the 5-state suppression machine (auth/credit flows differ; 2 states cover the real failures), and the memory subsystem (declined for now — the GOTCHAS/CONTEXT curation culture is the memory).

parts.text:
Since my environment's password doesn't match the plist's, I shouldn't read or print that password. Instead I should drive the compaction through the VM's serve over ssh, sourcing the env file on-box so the password never leaves the machine or appears in output.

I'll write a single ssh script: start a background curl capturing the SSE stream to a log file, create a session with a nonce title, run a haiku turn, trigger summarize, then grep the capture for the session.compacted frame, kill the curl process, and delete the session — bringing back only the frame line itself, since its content isn't sensitive. I just need to confirm python3 and curl are available on the box, which they should be on Ubuntu.

The Mac serve uses its own plist-scoped password, so I'll drive the boxbox VM's serve instead—working entirely over ssh, pulling the password from its env file without printing it, and handling capture and control in one script.

input.cmd:
ssh -n boxbox 'set -e; source ~/.config/cmx/env
AUTH="opencode:$OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD"
curl -sN -u "$AUTH" http://127.0.0.1:4096/event > /tmp/sse-cap.log 2>&1 &
CAPPID=$!
sleep 2
SID=$(curl -s -u "$AUTH" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4096/session -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{\"title\":\"compaction-wire-capture-nonce-x7q\"}" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"id\"])")
echo "SID=$SID"
curl -s -m 120 -u "$AUTH" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4096/session/$SID/message" -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{\"model\":{\"providerID\":\"anthropic\",\"modelID\":\"claude-haiku-4-5\"},\"agent\":\"build\",\"parts\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"reply with exactly: ok\"}]}" > /dev/null
curl -s -m 300 -u "$AUTH" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4096/session/$SID/summarize" -H "content-type: application/json" -d "{\"providerID\":\"anthropic\",\"modelID\":\"claude-haiku-4-5\"}"
echo " <- summarize rc"
sleep 3
kill $CAPPID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "--- frame:"
grep "session.compacted" /tmp/sse-cap.log | head -2
curl -s -m 10 -u "$AUTH" -X DELETE "http://127.0.0.1:4096/session/$SID" > /dev/null && echo "session deleted"
rm -f /tmp/sse-cap.log'

parts.text:
Everything's pushed and synced now — cmx and boxy-web are both at their latest commits on origin with clean bundles, and since both changes are docs/test fixtures with zero runtime impact, no serve restarts are needed.

For my answer, I'll give him a compact inventory of all documentation I updated, plus what I deliberately left untouched (prompt iterations, design.md, etc.) along with my reasoning for each.

Now yes — all of it. The honest inventory:

**cmx (`304eafab71`, pushed):**
- `CHANGES/2026-08-21-compaction-hardening.md` — the full record in house style: per-feature sections with file-level detail, the test/verification story, and a "deliberately not ported from grok-build" section so nobody re-litigates the ladder/segments/memory decisions later.
- `CHANGES/INDEX.md` — new fork-diff section for the drop (compaction.ts, config.ts, the three recall files, the regenerated SDK types), plus appends to the existing `prompt.ts` and `registry.ts` rows.
- `README.md` — a `recall` paragraph in the tool-surface section, linking the CHANGES file.
- GOTCHAS entries were already in from the build (`layer-pipe-20-arg-cap`, `dev-serve-event-sse`).

**boxy-web (`d778667`, pushed):**
- **Fixture re-pinned from a live frame** — the test file's own header demanded a real capture "the day the enriched serve is deployed," so I drove one more real compaction on the vm's serve and caught it on `/global/event`: `trigger:"manual", overflow:false, tokensBefore:33709, durationMs:1193, summaryChars:290`. That frame is now the pinned `enriched` fixture (12/12 tests, tsc clean); valid-`tailStartID` folding moved to the half-enriched case since a real tail-carrying frame needs a big session.
- `GOTCHAS.md` — the enriched wire shape with the verbatim capture, plus two traps the capture session itself paid for: the per-instance `/event` stayed silent while `/global/event` carried the frame, and `fleet.compaction` telemetry is **client-witnessed by design** — zero rows after the deploy is correct, not a bug (the schema doc says so; no tab was open).
- `CONTEXT.md` — the compaction-hardening block added to "cmx server knowledge" so no future agent re-derives the event shape, the prefire knob, or recall's existence.

**Judged not to need updating, with reasons:** the prompt-iteration line (`feat(prompts): iteration N`) tracks the prompt-system overhauls — this drop didn't iterate prompts (compaction.txt untouched; recall.txt is a tool description, covered by CHANGES/INDEX); `docs/design.md` is law, not a changelog — the gauge tick was built under it, not an amendment to it; boxbox `AGENTS.md`/`ops/deploy.md` — no new rules, commands, or deploy-flow changes.

Both doc commits are runtime-inert, so no serves were restarted; the vm and forge clones are synced to origin so the next binary deploy builds from a current tree. One thing deliberately left for real life rather than another synthetic drive: the pit seam pixels and the first client-witnessed `fleet.compaction` row — both land the first time a thread compacts while you're actually looking at boxbox.
